caption: The drawing depicts a single stoneware crock placed centrally on a plain, light beige background. The crock is cylindrical with a slightly wider upper rim and two small, curved handles on opposite sides near the top. The stoneware body is primarily a grayish-tan color with a matte texture. There are blue decorative marks on the front, resembling stylized leaves or abstract floral patterns, situated just below the handles. Above the blue decoration, there is dark blue text that reads: “W.M.E. WARNER WEST TROY,” stamped in an arc. A faint brownish discoloration or stain runs vertically down the surface from the rim to the base. The interior of the crock is a darker brown, visible from the top opening. The drawing is bordered by a plain paper margin, and the words "Crock Factory" are written in cursive in the lower left corner below the base of the crock.
title: Crock
cluster: #19 — Ceramic Arts: Pottery, Stoneware, and Porcelain
